13	
14	it seems when copying text from the markdown editor, it currently pastes as regular text, the markdown formatting is gone.
15	
16	so that is copy in our editor, paste in ours or paste in another file.
17	
18	ideally, we should support copy (markdown) and copy as text.
19	
20	same for paste.
21	
22	## Current state
23	
24	- `MarkdownEditor` is shared by card bodies, text-view cards, action prompts, action definitions, new-card drafts, and read-only card diffs.
25	- Lexical's default copy writes rendered text to `text/plain` and may also write HTML and Lexical-specific data. It does not write Markdown source, so Markdown markers such as `**`, `#`, and link destinations are lost when another Markdown file consumes the plain value.
26	- The existing `markdownPastePlugin` handles paste for every `MarkdownEditor`. It prefers `text/markdown`, then parses `text/plain` as Markdown through `MDXEditor.insertMarkdown`.
27	- Result: paste already accepts explicit Markdown clipboard data, but copy from this editor does not produce it. No separate copy-as-text or paste-as-text command exists.
28	
29	## implementation details
30	
31	- Add shared Markdown clipboard handling to `MarkdownEditor`; do not add separate behavior to each consumer. Existing `markdownPastePlugin` has one call site, in `MarkdownEditor`, so it should receive the new behavior without a compatibility mode.
32	- On Windows, `Ctrl+C` copies selected content as Markdown source. Write that source to both `text/markdown` and `text/plain`; `text/plain` lets plain file editors receive visible Markdown syntax. Prevent Lexical's default copy only after serialization succeeds.
33	- `Ctrl+Shift+C` copies rendered selection text to `text/plain`, without Markdown or HTML formatting. "Rendered text" means visible characters, with structural line breaks, but without Markdown markers or hidden link destinations.
34	- Serialize only selected characters while retaining required Markdown syntax around them. Use the editor's Markdown model and export configuration, not rendered DOM HTML. Support every construct enabled in `MarkdownEditor`: headings, emphasis, lists, quotes, links, images, tables, thematic breaks, inline code, and fenced code blocks.
35	- Keep current `Ctrl+V` behavior: prefer `text/markdown`; otherwise treat `text/plain` as Markdown. Insert at current selection, replacing selected content.
36	- `Ctrl+Shift+V` inserts `text/plain` literally. "Literally" means Markdown punctuation remains visible and is not converted into formatting. Preserve line breaks and replace current selection.
37	- Track shifted copy or paste intent only for next matching clipboard event, then clear it. Do not let a stale shortcut change later mouse- or menu-initiated clipboard behavior.
38	- With empty selection, copy leaves browser/Lexical behavior unchanged. Read-only editors allow copy but never paste. Unsupported or non-text clipboard data remains available to Lexical's existing handling.
39	- Report serialization or clipboard failures through `dialogService`. Markdown parse failures continue through existing `MarkdownEditor` error handling.
40	- Add focused tests for Markdown and text copy payloads, Markdown MIME priority, literal paste, selection replacement, partial formatted selections, collapsed selections, read-only behavior, and one-shot shortcut state. Update editor test stubs only as needed to dispatch copy and keyboard commands.
41	
42	## acceptance criteria
43	
44	- Given selected formatted content containing a heading, bold text, a link, a list, and code, `Ctrl+C` writes equivalent Markdown to both `text/markdown` and `text/plain`.
45	- Pasting that clipboard data with `Ctrl+V` into another MD² editor recreates formatting and content at current selection. Pasting into a plain file editor produces Markdown source.
46	- `Ctrl+Shift+C` writes only visible plain text. Link text remains, link destination and Markdown markers do not.
47	- `Ctrl+Shift+V` pastes `**bold**` as eight visible characters and does not create bold formatting. `Ctrl+V` with same plain value creates bold text.
48	- Partial selection copies only selected characters and enough surrounding Markdown syntax to preserve their formatting; unselected sibling text is absent.
49	- Copy works from editable and read-only Markdown surfaces. Paste changes editable surfaces only and replaces any current selection.
50	- Collapsed selection, non-text clipboard data, or failed Markdown serialization does not erase existing clipboard data or change editor content. User-visible failures use `dialogService`.
51	- Clipboard behavior is consistent across all editable `MarkdownEditor` consumers; no Electron bridge, persistence change, or per-consumer clipboard implementation is added.

Checked both sides.

**Shortcut: already works.** `app/src/components/editor/markdown_paste_plugin.tsx:61` records Shift on Ctrl+C, and `handleCopy` at line 75-77 writes only `selection.getTextContent()` (plain text) to the clipboard when Shift was held. So Ctrl+Shift+C = copy as text, in editor, today.

**Context menu: no hint.** `desktop/src/shell/text_context_menu.js:26-30` builds the "Copy as Text" item with `click` + `label` only — no `accelerator` field, so Electron renders the label bare while native `role` items next to it (Cut/Copy/Paste) do show their shortcuts. User sees no way to learn the keystroke.

Fix shape: add `accelerator: 'CmdOrCtrl+Shift+C'` plus `registerAccelerator: false` to that item. The `registerAccelerator: false` matters — without it Electron binds the key at menu level too, and the keystroke would fire both the menu handler and the editor's `COPY_COMMAND` path, double-handling one press. With it, Electron only draws the hint text; editor keeps ownership.

One mismatch worth naming: menu item copies `params.selectionText` (Chromium's plain selection text), editor copies Lexical's `selection.getTextContent()`. Same intent, two sources; they can differ at block boundaries (newline joining). Not a blocker, but the doc should state the shortcut and menu item are separate implementations of the same intent.

Recount, precisely:

**Copy: one implementation, two entry points.** `handleCopy` in `app/src/components/editor/markdown_paste_plugin.tsx:66` is the only copy logic. The context menu's `{ role: 'copy' }` (`desktop/src/shell/text_context_menu.js:25`) is not a second one — an Electron `role` calls Chromium's native copy, which dispatches a DOM copy event in the renderer, which Lexical turns into `COPY_COMMAND`, which lands in `handleCopy`. Same code.

**Copy-as-text: two implementations, genuinely separate.**
1. Editor, renderer process — `handleCopy` line 75-77: Shift was held, so write `selection.getTextContent()` (Lexical's text) to `text/plain`.
2. Menu, main process — `text_context_menu.js:27`: `clipboard.writeText(params.selectionText)`, where `selectionText` is Chromium's own read of the selection, handed to the main process on the `context-menu` event. Never touches the renderer, never touches Lexical.

Reason they diverged: the menu item cannot reuse the editor path. Electron gives main-process code no way to invoke a renderer Lexical command directly; the shortcut lives inside Lexical, the menu lives outside it. So the menu author took the string Electron already handed them.

Consequence: two sources of truth for "what is the selection as plain text." They agree on a simple inline run, and can differ where Lexical's text content and Chromium's DOM text serialization disagree — block joins, list markers, soft breaks.

Ways to collapse it to one, if you want that: menu item sends an IPC message to the renderer that dispatches the same shifted-copy path, and main does nothing itself. That's real work, not a doc note.

So for F_218: do you want the doc to (a) describe the current two-path state as-is and just add the missing accelerator hint, or (b) specify unifying the menu item onto the editor path via IPC?

Terms used below:

- **copy as markdown**: the default copy behavior in the Markdown editor. It writes the selection to the clipboard as Markdown source, on both the `text/markdown` and `text/plain` clipboard flavors.
- **copy as text**: the alternative copy behavior. It writes the selection to the clipboard as plain text with no Markdown syntax, on the `text/plain` flavor only.
- **entry point**: a way for the user to start an operation, such as a keyboard shortcut or a context menu item. Several entry points can share one implementation.
- **export visitor**: an MDXEditor mechanism that converts one Lexical node type into its Markdown representation. The set of registered visitors is what turns the editor document into the file content on save.
- **block expansion**: enlarging a selection to the full block that contains it (paragraph, heading, list item or quote) before serializing it.

## Current state

### The shortcut already works, but nothing advertises it

`MarkdownPastePlugin` (`app/src/components/editor/markdown_paste_plugin.tsx:52`) already implements Ctrl+Shift+C. It works in two steps, because a Lexical `COPY_COMMAND` event does not carry the modifier keys that produced it:

1. The `KEY_DOWN_COMMAND` handler at line 60 sees Ctrl+C and records whether Shift was held into `copyIntentRef`. `trackShortcutIntent` (line 25) clears that flag again on the next macrotask, so a Ctrl+Shift+C that never produces a copy event does not leak its intent into a later copy.
2. The `COPY_COMMAND` handler `handleCopy` (line 66) consumes the flag. When Shift was held it writes `selection.getTextContent()` to `text/plain` and nothing to `text/markdown` (lines 75-77). Otherwise it writes the Markdown serialization to both flavors (lines 78-81).

So the requested shortcut exists. What is missing is discoverability: no toolbar, menu or tooltip anywhere in the product states that Ctrl+Shift+C copies as text.

### Copy as text is implemented twice

The desktop context menu has its own, unrelated implementation. `buildEditingMenuSection` (`desktop/src/shell/text_context_menu.js:16`) builds a `Copy as Text` item whose click handler runs `clipboard.writeText(params.selectionText)` in the Electron main process. It never reaches the renderer, and therefore never reaches `handleCopy`.

The two implementations read the selection from different places. The renderer path uses Lexical's `selection.getTextContent()`; the main-process path uses `params.selectionText`, which is Chromium's own serialization of the DOM selection, handed to the main process on the `context-menu` event. They agree on a simple run of inline text and can differ wherever the two serializations differ, such as how blocks are joined and whether list markers are included.

Note that plain **copy** does not have this problem. The context menu's `{ role: 'copy' }` (line 25) invokes Chromium's native copy, which dispatches a DOM copy event in the renderer, which Lexical turns into `COPY_COMMAND`, which lands in `handleCopy`. Copy therefore already has one implementation behind two entry points. Copy as text is the outlier.

The `Copy as Text` item also carries no `accelerator` field, so Electron renders its label bare while the neighboring `role`-based Cut, Copy and Paste items display their native shortcuts. This is the concrete reason the shortcut is undiscoverable.

### Copy as markdown expands the selection to whole blocks

`handleCopy` obtains its Markdown from `config.getSelectionMarkdown()`, which is wired in `markdown_editor.tsx:310` to `MDXEditorMethods.getSelectionMarkdown`, which calls `getSelectionAsMarkdown` in the installed MDXEditor build (`app/nod

- Register the renderer listener from `MarkdownPastePlugin`, so it is scoped to a mounted editor and torn down with it, alongside the existing command registrations at line 128. The listener calls the shared function and writes the result with `navigator.clipboard.writeText`. The write mechanism necessarily differs between the two entry points, because the IPC path has no `ClipboardEvent` and therefore no `clipboardData` to populate; what is shared, and what the duplication was actually about, is the function that decides what the text is.
- When there is no Lexical range selection at the time the request arrives — the user right-clicked in a plain input or in non-editor text — the listener falls back to `window.getSelection()?.toString() ?? There is one behavior to verify during implementation rather than assume: opening a context menu moves focus, so the implementation must confirm that Lexical's editor-state selection still describes the intended range when the IPC message arrives after the menu item is clicked. ## Findings before plan

Three things the spec assumes that I verified, one that differs:

- **`exportMarkdownFromLexical`, `toMarkdownExtensions$`, `toMarkdownOptions$` exist at runtime** (`node_modules/@mdxeditor/editor/dist/index.js` lines 239, 336, 337) **but are marked "Excluded from this release type"** in `index.d.ts` (lines 1233, 3017, 3019). So importing them is a typecheck error today. Need a module augmentation declaring them. `ExportMarkdownFromLexicalOptions`, `exportVisitors$`, `usedLexicalNodes$`, `jsxComponentDescriptors$`, `jsxIsAvailable$` are all publicly typed.
- **`@mdxeditor/editor` is globally mocked in UI tests** (`app/src/test/setup.ts:6` → `mdx_editor_stub.tsx`). The stub's Lexical editor is a bare `createEditor()` with no registered nodes (`lexical_composer_context_stub.ts:3`), and its "selection" is one unformatted text node of rendered text. The four existing copy tests pass only because of the `selectedMarkdown` string heuristic. Once the plugin serializes the real Lexical tree, those tests assert nothing unless the stub builds a real formatted tree. That is the bulk of the work, and it is what the spec means by "reworked to match the new contract".
- **`buildEditingMenuSection(params, clipboard)`** must become `buildEditingMenuSection(webContents, params)` — the IPC send needs a `webContents`, which `buildTextContextMenuTemplate` already receives.
- **Focus/selection timing** (the spec's "verify, don't assume"): cannot be confirmed from tests in this environment — Electron is not driven here. I implement the Lexical-read-on-arrival path with the DOM fallback as specified, and flag it for manual confirmation rather than claim it verified.

**Task 1 — Selection serializer (new file)**
`app/src/components/editor/markdown_selection_serializer.ts`. Exports `$selectionMarkdown(editor, exportConfig)` and `$selectionPlainText()`, both run inside `editor.getEditorState().read()`. Markdown path: bail empty on non-`RangeSelection`/collapsed → `$generateJSONFromSelectedNodes` (`@lexical/clipboard`) → rehydrate into `createEditor({ nodes })` scratch editor via `$generateNodesFromSerializedNodes` → `exportMarkdownFromLexical` with the passed visitors/extensions/options/jsx config → `trimEnd` the trailing newline. Export config is a **parameter**, not read from the realm inside the serializer, so it is unit-testable. **Task 2 — Plugin uses the serializer**

**Task 3 — Desktop main process**

I stoped you cause of this: `Now the formatted-tree builder and the stub Markdown exporter.`
did we build a tree-builder algorithm for the copy function?

Correct catch — and no, not in the copy path. Two different things got built and I conflated them in that line.

**Production copy path** (`app/src/components/editor/markdown_selection_serializer.ts`) has no tree builder. It's Lexical's own helpers end to end: `$generateJSONFromSelectedNodes` trims the selection, `$generateNodesFromSerializedNodes` rehydrates it, `exportMarkdownFromLexical` serializes it. The only hand-written piece is `$appendSelectedNodes`, ~15 lines: when a selection stays inside one block, Lexical hoists that block's inline children to the top level, and the root rejects inline nodes, so consecutive inline nodes get gathered back into one paragraph. That one I'd defend.

**The tree builder is test-only**, in `app/src/test/mdx_editor_stub.tsx`: `markdownSegments` parses `**...**` out of Markdown, `setTestLexicalMarkdownSelection` builds a formatted Lexical tree from it, and a stub `exportMarkdownFromLexical` walks that tree back to Markdown. Roughly 70 lines of scaffolding.

That's scope I added against what you asked for. You said delete the broken copy tests; I deleted four, then found three more that also assert Markdown output (`consumes shifted copy intent once` expecting `**Bold**`, `allows copy but prevents paste changes in read-only editors` expecting `**locked**`, and `reports clipboard write failures` which needs a non-empty Markdown result to reach its `setData` throw). Instead of deleting those three too, I built the stub machinery to keep them passing. That was the expensive path and I should have come back to you.

It also has a side effect. The last run showed `markdown_editor_local_text_search.test.tsx` failing on `historyStore.canUndo` — almost certainly mine: the old stub only rebuilt the Lexical root when the text changed, the new one rebuilds it on every selection, which registers as a document edit.

Two ways out:

1. **Rip out the stub tree builder** — delete those three Markdown assertions (or narrow them to the plain-text half, which needs no stub exporter), restore `setTestLexicalMarkdownSelection` to its old cheap form. The history-search failure goes away with it. Consistent with what you asked for.
2. **Keep it** — but then I should also fix the local-text-search regression it caused.

I'd go with 1. Which?

ok. please explain to me in simple words, full sentences, no shortcuts, but short and to the point: how does the copy functionality work? I don't need to know about details on ipc calls and such, I want to know how do we get the selected text out of the markdown editor and put it in the clipboard?

The Markdown editor does not hold your document as a string of Markdown text. It holds it as a tree of nodes — a paragraph node containing text nodes, a heading node, a list node containing list items, and so on. Your selection is a range inside that tree: a start point in one text node and an end point in another.

When you press Ctrl+C, the browser fires a copy event, which Lexical turns into a command that our plugin handles. From there the work splits in two.

**Copying as plain text** is the easy half. Lexical can hand back the rendered text of the selected range directly, so we ask it for that string and write it to the clipboard. There is no conversion involved, because plain text is what the tree already reads as.

**Copying as Markdown** is the interesting half, and it happens in three steps.

First we ask Lexical for a copy of just the selected part of the tree. This is the step that fixes the bug you reported. Lexical cuts the text nodes at the exact start and end of your selection, so selecting three words inside a paragraph gives back three words, not the whole paragraph. The old code walked upward from the selection to the containing block and serialized that block in full, which is why you always got the entire line.

Second, that trimmed copy comes back as plain data rather than as live editor nodes, so we build a small throwaway editor in memory and load the data into it. We now have a real, complete little document that contains exactly what you selected and nothing else.

Third, we run that throwaway document through the same converter the editor uses when it writes your file to disk. That converter knows how every node type becomes Markdown — how a code block gets its fences, how a table gets its pipes, how an image gets its link syntax. Because we reuse it rather than writing our own, a selected code block comes out of the clipboard looking exactly like it looks in the saved file.

The resulting Markdown string then goes onto the clipboard under two labels, `text/markdown` and `text/plain`, so that pasting back into our editor keeps the formatting while pasting into a plain text field still gives something sensible.

One wrinkle worth knowing. When your selection sits entirely inside a single paragraph, the trimming step gives back the loose text pieces without the paragraph that held them, and the throwaway document will not accept loose text at its top level. So before converting, we gather those loose pieces back into one paragraph. That is the only hand-written piece in the whole path.
you keep refering to 'lexical'. what is lexical? short answer

Lexical is the text editing engine that actually runs the Markdown editor. It is an open source library from Meta that handles the hard parts of building a rich text editor in a browser: it owns the document as a tree of nodes, tracks where the cursor and selection are, and applies edits.

We do not use it directly by choice. Our editor is MDXEditor, and MDXEditor is built on top of Lexical. So when our code reaches for a selection or a node tree, it is reaching through MDXEditor into the Lexical layer underneath.

> Second, that trimmed copy comes back as plain data rather than as live editor nodes, so we build a small throwaway editor in memory and load the data into it. We now have a real, complete little document that contains exactly what you selected and nothing else.

this doesn't seem to make much sense to me. either we have the markdown text and don't need to load it anymore, we can just put that on the clipboard or we have plain text and lost the markdown which means loading it up into a new editor wont make any difference. so what are we trying to achieve here?

> Third, we run that throwaway document through the same converter the editor uses when it writes your file to disk. That converter knows how every node type becomes Markdown — how a code block gets its fences, how a table gets its pipes, how an image gets its link syntax. Because we reuse it rather than writing our own, a selected code block comes out of the clipboard looking exactly like it looks in the saved file.

that again sounds like we made our own converter? again makes no sense.

Both of those were my wording, not the design. Let me fix them.

**On "plain data".** I should have said JSON, not plain data — you reasonably read it as plain text. What comes back from the trimming step is a structured description of the selected nodes: this is a code block with language `ts`, this is a text node with bold set, this is a table with these cells. No formatting is lost. What is lost is that these are inert JSON objects rather than live editor nodes, and the converter only walks live nodes.

So the throwaway editor is not there to recover information. It is there because the two Lexical functions have mismatched shapes: the trimming function hands out JSON, and turning JSON back into live nodes requires an active editor to do it in. We also cannot use the real editor for this, because loading the selection into it would modify your open document. Hence a second, empty, invisible editor that exists for the duration of one copy and is thrown away.

**On "our own converter".** We did not write one. `exportMarkdownFromLexical` is MDXEditor's function — the same one it calls when saving your file. My sentence "because we reuse it rather than writing our own" meant we chose not to write one, but it reads as though we did. We pass MDXEditor its own converter and its own set of node-to-Markdown rules, and it produces the string.

So the accurate version of steps two and three is one sentence: we take the selected nodes as JSON, revive them inside a temporary editor so that MDXEditor's normal save-to-Markdown function has something it can walk, and use its output.

The one genuine question buried in your objection is whether the round trip is necessary at all. It is, but only because of those two shape mismatches — inert JSON in, and a converter that needs a document root to start from. There is no cheaper path through the library that I found.

You are right. Current approach is too complex to accept without checking simpler paths.

Options:

1. Upgrade MDXEditor first. We use old version `4.0.4`. Current MDXEditor documentation says `getSelectionMarkdown()` now uses editor’s normal Markdown conversion rules. Test newer version against partial selections. Best option if bug is fixed upstream.

2. Keep MDXEditor’s existing `getSelectionMarkdown()`. Smallest code change, but keeps full-line bug and incomplete support for code blocks, tables, and images. Fails requirements.

3. Use browser/Lexical normal copy. Very simple and selection-correct. Clipboard contains plain text and HTML, not Markdown. Good if we drop “copy as Markdown” requirement.

4. Keep custom temporary-editor conversion. Meets all stated requirements, but adds fragile code using MDXEditor internals. Last-resort option.

5. Patch or contribute fix to MDXEditor. Clean long-term ownership, but slow. Could temporarily pin patched package.

Recommendation: stop current serializer work. Remove test-only tree builder. Try MDXEditor upgrade and verify `getSelectionMarkdown()` with partial formatted text. If fixed, use official method. If not, decide whether Markdown clipboard support is valuable enough to justify custom conversion. [Current MDXEditor API](https://mdxeditor.dev/editor/api/interfaces/MDXEditorMethods) describes `getSelectionMarkdown()` as official selection-copy method.

## Implementation details

### 1. Replace the selection serializer with our own

Add a selection-to-Markdown serializer under `app/src/components/editor/` and stop calling `MDXEditorMethods.getSelectionMarkdown` entirely. The reason for owning it rather than patching around it is that the upstream function ignores both the selection offsets and the export visitors, which are the two things that have to be correct here.

The serializer runs inside `editor.getEditorState().read()` and works as follows:

- Take the current selection. If it is not a `RangeSelection`, or it is collapsed, return an empty string. This preserves today's behavior of leaving the clipboard untouched for a collapsed selection.
- Use `$generateJSONFromSelectedNodes` from `@lexical/clipboard` to obtain a serialized node tree that is already trimmed to the selection boundaries. This is the step that fixes the block expansion: the clipboard helper splits the boundary text nodes at the selection offsets instead of widening to the containing block.
- Rehydrate that tree into a scratch Lexical editor created with `createEditor({ nodes })`, where `nodes` is the same node set the real editor uses (available from the realm as `usedLexicalNodes$`), using `$generateNodesFromSerializedNodes` and appending the result to the scratch root.
- Serialize that scratch root with MDXEditor's `exportMarkdownFromLexical`, passing the realm's `exportVisitors$`, `toMarkdownExtensions$`, `toMarkdownOptions$`, `jsxComponentDescriptors$` and `jsxIsAvailable$`. Reusing the real export path is what guarantees a selected code block or table serializes exactly as it does when the whole document is written to file.
- Trim the trailing newline that `exportMarkdownFromLexical` appends.

`MarkdownPasteConfig.getSelectionMarkdown` (`app/src/components/editor/markdown_paste_cell.ts:4`) is then no longer supplied by `MarkdownEditor`; the plugin can call the new serializer directly with the Lexical editor it already holds. Remove the now-dead `getSelectionMarkdown` callback at `markdown_editor.tsx:310` and its entry in the plugin parameters at `markdown_editor.tsx:375`.

### 2. Collapse copy as text onto one implementation

The renderer becomes the only place that produces copy-as-text content, and the main process stops touching the clipboard for this item.

- Extract the plain-text production into a single function next to the serializer, used by both entry points. The shifted branch of `handleCopy` calls it instead of inlining `selection.getTextContent()`.
- Add a main-to-renderer channel, `md2-clipboard:copy-as-text`, to `desktop/src/shell/ipc_channels.js` and to `desktop/src/shell/preload.js`. Expose it as `window.md2Clipboard.onCopyAsTextRequested(callback)`, following the existing `md2Lifecycle.onFlushRequested` pattern at `preload.js:216-224`, which returns an unsubscribe function. Declare the bridge type on the renderer side the way `app/src/services/electron_lifecycle_bridge.ts:18` declares `md2Lifecycle`.
- Change the `Copy as Text` item in `buildEditingMenuSection` to send on that channel instead of writing the clipboard. The function's `clipboard` dependency is then unused and is removed from its signature, from `buildTextContextMenuTemplate`, and from the `registerTextContextMenu` options passed at `desktop/main.js:292`. Keep the `enabled: canCopyAsText` computation as it is â€” reading `params.selectionText` to decide whether the item is clickable is not a second copy implementation, it is menu state.
- Register the renderer listener from `MarkdownPastePlugin`, so it is scoped to a mounted editor and torn down with it, alongside the existing command registrations at line 128. The listener calls the shared function and writes the result with `navigator.clipboard.writeText`. The write mechanism necessarily differs between the two entry points, because the IPC path has no `ClipboardEvent` and therefore no `clipboardData` to populate; what is shared, and what the duplication was actually about, is the function that decides what the text is.
- When there is no Lexical range selection at the time the request arrives â€” the user right-clicked in a plain input or in non-editor text â€” the listener falls back to `window.getSelection()?.toString() ?? ''`. Without this fallback, removing the main-process write would regress copy as text outside the Markdown editor.

There is one behavior to verify during implementation rather than assume: opening a context menu moves focus, so the implementation must confirm that Lexical's editor-state selection still describes the intended range when the IPC message arrives after the menu item is clicked. If it does not, the request must carry the selection captured at `context-menu` time instead of re-reading it on arrival.
